profile.summary: Orca predicts the three-dimensional folding of the human genome from DNA sequence alone. It takes a genomic sequence of up to 256 Mb and returns predicted contact matrices at nine scales, from 4 kb resolution within 1 Mb up to whole-chromosome distances. It is used to run in silico Hi-C experiments: to ask what a structural variant, a haplotype or a designed sequence would do to local and large-scale genome structure.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: What is Orca, What can I use Orca for; paper: Results, Sequence-based prediction of multiscale 3D genome interactions

summary_quotes.text: Orca can **predict genome interactions from kilobase to whole-chromosome-scales** using only genomic sequence as input.
the maximum input size 256Mb, which is larger than the largest human chromosome
an entire assembled genome,  or any sequence you wish to perform an in silico Hi-C experiment on
a ‘zooming’-like cascading prediction mechanism was designed to enable the prediction of ultra-long-distance interactions to shorter distance interactions with nine different resolutions
down to 4-kb resolution interactions within 1-Mb distance at the bottom level

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Orca has a hierarchical sequence encoder and a cascade of decoders. The encoder turns a one-hot sequence into representations at nine resolutions, from 4 kb up to 1,024 kb. Each decoder predicts one 250 by 250 interaction matrix for a window of a given size, as a log fold change over a distance-based background. The decoders run from the top down: each lower level takes the sequence representation at its resolution, the prediction from the level above cropped and upsampled, and a pairwise distance encoding matrix. Encoder and decoders are convolutional with residual connections; each decoder has 112 convolution layers cycling through dilation factors 1 to 64. Predictions are symmetrised with their transpose and averaged between the forward and reverse-complement sequence. The encoder is also trained on an auxiliary task of predicting DNase-seq and ChIP-seq chromatin profiles.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Orca model architecture for multiscale 3D genome prediction

quotes.text: The Orca model architecture is composed of a hierarchical sequence encoder and a multi-level cascading decoder
All predicted interaction matrices are of size 250 × 250 and all predicted scores represent log fold over distance-based background.
the upper sections of the encoder create a series of sequence encoding at 4-kb, 8-kb, …, 1024-kb resolutions
The 2D convolution blocks cycle through dilation factors of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 for four full passes with a total of 112 convolution layers per decoder.
The final model prediction is symmetrized by averaging with its transpose.
The model predictions are averaged between the predictions from the forward and the reverse-complement sequences.
The sequence encoder is also trained with an auxiliary task of predicting DNase-seq and ChIP-seq chromatin profile labels

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Orca is a framework with several models, not one checkpoint. Separate models were trained per dataset: H1-ESC and HFF from micro-C, and a cohesin-depleted HCT116 Hi-C model used for the compartment analysis. The README loads models by scale, named 1M, 32M and 256M, and offers the 1 Mb model as the faster option for sub-megabase screens. A result should name the cell-type model and the scale, and the repository commit, since the weights come as Zenodo resource tarballs rather than from a versioned model hub. The training code for the three stages is in the train directory.
sections.source_locator: README: What is Orca, Basic Usage, Orca-1Mb model, Train Orca models; paper: Methods, Model training and evaluation

quotes.text: Orca models are trained on high-resolution micro-C datasets for H1-ESC and HFF cell lines (and a cohesin-depleted HCT116 Hi-C model for the analysis of sequence dependencies of chromatin compartments).
orca_predict.load_resources(models=['32M', '256M'])
orca_predict.load_resources(models=["1M"])
If you are running a larger scale virtural screen that focus mostly on  <1Mb structures, Orca-1Mb model offers better speed.
A separate model was trained for each micro-C dataset.
Each model is trained in three stages (1Mb module, 1-32Mb module, 32-256Mb module), corresponding to the three python files.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised convolutional sequence-to-contact-map model for 3D genome structure.
facts.source_locator: README: Orca; paper: Methods, Orca model architecture

quotes.text: a deep learning sequence modeling framework for multiscale genome structure prediction
Both the encoder and decoders are convolutional networks with residual connections.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Hierarchical 1D convolutional encoder at nine resolutions (4 kb to 1,024 kb) plus a cascade of 2D dilated convolutional decoders, 112 convolution layers each, with residual connections.

quotes.text: The hierarchical sequence encoder alternates between 1D residual convolution blocks and max-pooling layers.
a series of sequence encoding at 4-kb, 8-kb, …, 1024-kb resolutions
a total of 112 convolution layers per decoder
The 2D convolution architecture consists of 2D residual convolution blocks with the linear+nonlinear path design.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: One-hot encoded human DNA sequence, up to 256 Mb, plus the position to zoom into and, at the 32 Mb to 256 Mb levels, distance encoding matrices. Multichromosomal input is allowed at those levels.
facts.source_locator: README: Basic Usage; paper: Methods and Results

quotes.text: The encoder computation starts from a bottom-up pass (high resolution to low resolution) starting from raw sequence with one-hot encoding
outputs = genomepredict(Genome.sequence_to_encoding(sequence)[None,:,:], chrom, mpos=pos, wpos=wpos, use_cuda=True)
#mpos: specifies the coordinate to zoom into for multiscale prediction
Interchromosomal interactions are also allowed at 32Mb–256Mb levels by using multichromosomal input

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A series of 250 by 250 predicted interaction matrices, one per scale, as log fold over a distance-based background, for H1-ESC and HFF. The CLI also writes pdf plots and a .pth dictionary with predictions, observed data, coordinates and annotations.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Methods, Orca model architecture; README: Example output

quotes.text: All predicted interaction matrices are of size 250 × 250 and all predicted scores represent log fold over distance-based background.
`predictions` - Multi-level predictions for H1-ESC and HFF cell types.
the output includes graphical visualizations in pdf format and numerical results saved in pytorch serialization format

facts.value: Not reported. The sources read give layer counts and channel widths but no total parameter count.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Micro-C for H1-ESC (4DN 4DNFI9GMP2J8) and HFF (4DNFI643OYP9), plus cohesin-depleted HCT116 Hi-C (4DNFILP99QJS), with sequence from GRCh38/hg38. Training samples were drawn on the fly from training chromosomes; some chromosomes were held out as a test set.

strengths.text: One model covers scales from 4 kb up to a whole chromosome, so local structure and compartments can be read from the same prediction.

run_guide.summary: Build the conda environment and the patched Selene library, get the Orca code and the core resource package, then predict interactions for one genomic region.
prerequisites: conda or miniconda. The environment pins python=3.9 and installs gcc, cooltools and cython, then PyTorch, then the packages in part 2.
PyTorch installed separately following the PyTorch installation guide, for CPU or GPU as appropriate.
A GPU is the default. The README says CPU may be enough for a few variants or the 1 Mb model, and recommends a GPU with over 8GB RAM for more than a couple of dozen variants.
Academic research use only under the repository licence.
Disk for the resource packages: 1.3G for the core package, 34G for the micro-C package and 15G for the extra tracks.

steps.title: Predict one region with the command line interface
steps.explanation: The CLI's region mode, with the coordinate format and the required output directory as the README gives them. Add --nocuda to run on CPU, or --256m for the 256 Mb models.

quotes.text: orca_predict region [options] <coordinate> <output_dir>
requires specifying a region as input in the format like `chr9:94904000-126904000`
--nocuda        Use CPU implementation.

outputs: pdf visualisations of the multi-level predictions and a .pth file holding a dictionary with predictions, matching micro-C observations where available, chromosome name, start and end coordinates per level, and annotations.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The clone comes first here so that the environment files exist; the README lists the environment steps before the clone.
The checkout line is an addition; the README gives a plain clone.
The CLI invocation is written as python orca_predict.py, following the README's usage block, which names the file but prints the usage without the python prefix.
The README notes that running in CPU mode on a machine that has a CUDA device can error in torch.DataParallel, and to prefix the command with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= in that case.

notes: Orca is a framework with several models (H1-ESC, HFF, cohesin-depleted HCT116, each at 1M, 32M and 256M), so the record is best kept at family level. The licence is a custom academic-use-only licence, not an SPDX identifier, which is why no licence field is set on the repository sources and their bytes are not stored. The paper full text from Europe PMC is under a view and text-mine licence, so its bytes are not stored either. The existing GenBench source was not re-fetched.
